title: What training is mandatory for employers in the United States?
seoTitle: Mandatory training in the United States
description: Mandatory employer training in the US by theme: OSHA, state harassment laws, HIPAA and cyber rules, BSA/AML, FINRA and licensing CE, CMS health care and DOT.
shortAnswer: As at November 2026, the United States has no single mandatory training law. Federal OSHA standards require hazard specific training, such as hazard communication and annual bloodborne pathogens training. Sector regulators add duties for banks, broker-dealers, health care providers, federal contractors and transport employers. States add harassment, workplace violence and licensing rules, so the obligations depend on industry, workforce size and the states where employees work.
keyTakeaways: Federal training duties are set standard by standard: OSHA has no general training rule but dozens of hazard specific ones, several with annual refreshers.

State law adds the most visible employer wide duties: harassment training every two years in California and annually in New York and Illinois, and workplace violence prevention training in California and New York retail.

Regulated industries carry fixed cycles, such as FINRA's annual Regulatory Element, 8 hours of annual CE for mortgage loan originators, annual Medicare compliance training and quarterly security awareness under NERC CIP-004.
Many federal rules require training without an interval, for example BSA/AML 'training for appropriate personnel' and HIPAA privacy training; regulators and examiners then judge adequacy.
Professional CE runs on state cycles that differ by profession and state, so a multistate employer tracks renewal periods per license, not per course.

sections.heading: How are mandatory training duties set in the United States?

blocks.text: US training duties come from four sources: federal agency regulations (OSHA, DOT, FDA, CMS, banking agencies, FinCEN), self regulatory organizations such as FINRA, conditions attached to federal funding or program participation (Medicare, Title IV student aid, federal grants), and state law. There is no general federal duty to train; each obligation attaches to a hazard, an activity or a regulated status, and the employer must assemble its own list.

OSHA shows the pattern. Its standards set training duties hazard by hazard, often with initial and annual requirements, as in bloodborne pathogens training at initial assignment and at least annually ([29 CFR 1910.1030](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-B/chapter-XVII/part-1910/section-1910.1030)). About half the states run OSHA-approved State Plans that must be at least as effective and can add rules, such as California's written Injury and Illness Prevention Program ([8 CCR 3203](https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3203.html)).

Enforcement expectations matter as much as rules. The Department of Justice evaluates whether corporate training is "appropriately tailored" when it decides how to resolve criminal cases ([DOJ](https://www.justice.gov/media/1160391/dl?inline)), and banking examiners assess training adequacy where the regulation sets no interval. The tables below cover every US regulation page in this library, grouped by theme, as at November 2026; closely related state pages share a row. The [Australia hub](/guides/mandatory-workplace-training-in-australia) shows a comparable federal and state structure.

sections.heading: What OSHA training applies in general industry?

blocks.text: General industry employers must train employees on each hazard an OSHA standard covers in their workplace, typically at initial assignment and again when tasks or hazards change. Some standards add annual refreshers, including bloodborne pathogens, respiratory protection, hearing conservation, lead, asbestos and fire extinguishers.

blocks.text: The annual standards cluster around health hazards. Respiratory protection requires retraining annually and whenever changes make prior training obsolete ([29 CFR 1910.134](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1910.134)); HAZWOPER requires eight hours of refresher training annually ([29 CFR 1910.120](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1910.120)); hazard communication, by contrast, has no refresher interval and is retriggered only by new hazards ([29 CFR 1910.1200](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1910.1200)).

sections.heading: What construction, state safety and workplace violence training is required?

blocks.text: Construction employers must train workers exposed to falls, scaffolds, silica and cranes, and crane operators must be certified. Several states add employer wide programs, including California's injury and illness prevention and workplace violence plans and New York's retail worker safety training.

blocks.text: California's workplace violence law shows how fast state duties can arrive. Labor Code 6401.9 has been enforceable since July 1, 2024, requiring initial training and annual training thereafter, and the standards board must adopt a general industry standard by December 31, 2026 ([Cal/OSHA](https://www.dir.ca.gov/dosh/dosh_publications/WPV-General-Industry-for-employers-fs.pdf)). New York's retail law differs by size: retail employers with 50 or more employees train annually, smaller ones every two years ([NYS DOL](https://dol.ny.gov/retail-workplace-violence-prevention-training)).

blocks.text: Mining, nuclear, laboratory and environmental rules set training or certification for people handling specific hazards. Several set fixed refreshers, such as 8 hours of annual refresher training for miners and pesticide worker training every 12 months.

sections.heading: What harassment, ethics and nondiscrimination training is required?

blocks.text: No federal law requires private employers to provide harassment training, but several states do: California every two years for employers with five or more employees, and New York and Illinois annually. Federal duties cover federal employees, education institutions and health programs receiving federal funds, and enforcement policy rewards effective anti corruption training.

blocks.text: State laws drive most multistate harassment programs. California requires two hours for supervisors and one hour for other employees every two years ([Gov. Code 12950.1](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12950.1)); New York requires interactive training annually ([Labor Law 201-g](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/LAB/201-G)); Illinois requires every employee to be trained each calendar year by December 31 ([IDHR](https://dhr.illinois.gov/about-us/idhr-faqs/training-faqs.html)).

sections.heading: What privacy, cybersecurity and records training is required?

blocks.text: Privacy and security training duties attach to sectors: HIPAA for health care, Gramm-Leach-Bliley rules for financial institutions, FCC rules for telecom carriers, and NIST based controls for federal agencies and contractors. Annual intervals are common in federal and state cybersecurity rules, and the electric sector requires quarterly security awareness.

blocks.text: The electric sector has the tightest cycle in this library. NERC CIP-004-7 requires security awareness that reinforces cyber security practices at least once each calendar quarter, and cyber security training before access and at least once every 15 calendar months ([NERC](https://www.nerc.com/pa/Stand/Reliability%20Standards/CIP-004-7.pdf)). For financial services in New York, 23 NYCRR 500.14 requires awareness training at least annually for all personnel ([Cornell LII](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-york/23-NYCRR-500.14)). HIPAA sets triggers instead ([45 CFR 164.530](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.530)).

sections.heading: What AML, sanctions and export control training is required?

blocks.text: The Bank Secrecy Act requires every covered financial institution's AML program to include an ongoing employee training program, without setting an interval. Sanctions and export control training is expected rather than mandated, and OFAC's framework says training should be provided at a minimum annually.

blocks.text: BSA rules are framed as a program pillar. The current regulations require "training for appropriate personnel", and FinCEN's April 2026 proposed rule would keep an ongoing employee training program with a proposed effective date 12 months after a final rule ([Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/04/10/2026-07033/anti-money-laundering-and-countering-the-financing-of-terrorism-programs)). OFAC goes further than the BSA on frequency, stating that training should be provided periodically "and at a minimum, annually" ([OFAC](https://ofac.treasury.gov/media/16331/download?inline)).

blocks.text: FINRA's two part structure is a useful model. The Regulatory Element is completed annually by December 31 for each registration category, and the Firm Element requires an annual needs evaluation and written training plan ([FINRA Rule 1240](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/rulebooks/finra-rules/1240)). Mortgage loan originators need at least 8 hours of approved CE each year, including 3 hours of federal law, with no carry forward ([12 CFR 1008.107](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-X/part-1008/subpart-B/section-1008.107)).

sections.heading: Which licensed professions carry continuing education cycles?

blocks.text: State licensing boards set continuing education for accountants, lawyers, physicians, nurses, pharmacists, EMS clinicians, real estate agents and security guards, each on its own cycle and with state specific mandatory topics. Federal law adds a one-time 8 hour substance use disorder training for DEA registered practitioners.

Laboratories, device and drug manufacturers, and state licensed facilities add their own rules.

blocks.text: CMS rules are conditions of participation. Nurse aides need at least 12 hours of in-service training a year, covering dementia management and abuse prevention ([42 CFR 483.95](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/483.95)). Laboratories run a tighter cycle: CLIA competency must be evaluated at least semiannually in an employee's first year and annually after that ([42 CFR 493.1413](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-493/subpart-M/section-493.1413)).

blocks.text: Colleges receiving federal student aid must train the officials who handle sexual misconduct cases, and child care programs funded by the federal government require pre-service health and safety training. Food businesses need certified managers and trained workers under FDA rules, and tobacco retailers earn lower penalties with approved training programs.

sections.heading: What training do US transport employers need?

blocks.text: DOT agencies require training for anyone handling hazardous materials, new commercial drivers, supervisors who make reasonable suspicion drug and alcohol decisions, and pipeline workers performing covered tasks. Airline crew training follows FAA approved programs with recurrent cycles of 6 to 12 months.

blocks.text: Hazmat training is one of the few cross-industry DOT rules. Any employer that ships, prepares or transports hazardous materials must train hazmat employees within 90 days of employment or a job change and provide recurrent training at least every three years ([49 CFR 172.704](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-172.704)). Airline crew run much shorter cycles, with recurrent training within the preceding 12 calendar months ([14 CFR 121.433](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-121.433)).

sections.heading: How should a US employer build a single training register?

blocks.text: Build the US register in three layers: federal obligations by regulated activity, state obligations by the states where employees work, and individual license cycles. Most errors come from applying one company wide annual cycle to rules that run on triggers, two or three year cycles, or license renewal dates.

items: **List regulated activities, not departments.** Chemical exposure, respirator use, forklifts, hazmat shipping, Medicare participation, broker-dealer registration and federal contracts each bring a distinct rule.

**Map employees to states.** Harassment, workplace violence, heat illness and injury prevention duties follow the employee's work location; California, New York and Illinois alone produce three different harassment cycles.

**Record each interval exactly as written.** Distinguish annual (bloodborne pathogens, NYDFS, FINRA Regulatory Element), every two or three years (California harassment, DOT hazmat, PSM refreshers), quarterly (NERC CIP-004), trigger based (hazard communication, HIPAA) and no interval (BSA/AML). Where none is set, record the risk rationale using [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).
**Track licenses per person and state.** CPA, legal, medical, nursing, pharmacy, real estate, insurance and EMS renewals run on individual dates.
**Separate rules from enforcement expectations.** DOJ, OFAC, BIS and banking examiner expectations are not regulations but determine how training failures are judged.

**Apply record retention per rule.** Bloodborne pathogens training records 3 years, FTA training records 2 years, worker protection records 2 years, California harassment records at least 2 years. See [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each obligation with its federal or state source, trigger and interval, so a multistate employer can see which rule drives each learning outcome for each population. When a source changes, such as a new state law or a final FinCEN rule, the affected outcomes and roles are identified directly. The [audit evidence](/platform/audit-evidence) page describes how this evidence is held.

faqs.q: Is there a federal law requiring annual compliance training for all employers?
faqs.a: No. Annual intervals appear only in specific rules, such as OSHA bloodborne pathogens and respiratory protection, FINRA's Regulatory Element, Medicare Advantage compliance training and New York's cybersecurity regulation. Many federal rules, including BSA/AML and HIPAA, require training without setting an interval.

faqs.q: Do private employers have to provide sexual harassment training?
faqs.a: Not under federal law. Several states require it, including California every two years for employers with five or more employees, New York annually for all employers, and Illinois annually by December 31. Multistate employers usually adopt one program that meets the strictest applicable state.

faqs.q: Do OSHA State Plan states have different training rules?
faqs.a: They can. State Plans must be at least as effective as federal OSHA and may add requirements, such as California's written Injury and Illness Prevention Program and heat illness training. Employers in those states follow the state rules, which generally include the federal topics.

faqs.q: How should employers handle training rules with no set frequency?
faqs.a: Where a regulation requires training without an interval, as BSA/AML and HIPAA privacy rules do, set a frequency based on risk, role and change, document the rationale, and retrain on triggers such as new procedures or incidents. Examiners and enforcement agencies judge whether the program is effective, not whether a particular interval was chosen.
